title: Understanding Membership Inference Attacks on EEG Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.28354v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) signals contain sensitive, subject-specific information, making models trained on them potential targets for membership inference attacks (MIAs). Although MIAs have been studied extensively in other domains, their applications to EEG models are relatively scarce, and the factors driving the vulnerability of EEG models to MIAs are not adequately understood. In this paper, we present a systematic empirical analysis of MIAs on EEG models using three datasets, seven model architectures, four attack methods, and two metrics. Results show that poor model generalization (large train-test loss and accuracy gap) is the strongest indicator of MIA vulnerability. Longer training and larger models also increase vulnerability. Moreover, no particular scalp region, frequency band, inter-channel correlation pattern, or temporal versus spectral representation of EEG data consistently explains MIA vulnerability across datase

translated_title: 理解脑电图（EEG）模型上的成员推理攻击
translated_abstract: 脑电图（EEG）信号包含敏感的受试者特定信息，使得在其上训练的模型可能成为成员推理攻击（MIA）的目标。尽管MIA在其他领域已被广泛研究，但其在EEG模型中的应用相对稀少，且导致EEG模型对MIA脆弱性的因素尚未得到充分理解。在本文中，我们使用三个数据集、七种模型架构、四种攻击方法和两个指标，对EEG模型上的MIA进行了系统的实证分析。结果表明，模型泛化能力差（训练与测试之间的损失和准确率差距大）是MIA脆弱性的最强指标。更长的训练时间和更大的模型也会增加脆弱性。此外，没有任何特定的头皮区域、频段、通道间相关性模式，或EEG数据的时间与频谱表示，能够在各数据集间一致地解释MIA脆弱性。
tldr: 本研究通过对多个数据集、模型架构和攻击方法的系统实验，发现EEG模型对成员推理攻击的脆弱性主要由模型泛化能力差决定，更长的训练和更大的模型也会加剧这一风险，而EEG数据本身的空间、频率或表征特征并不能一致地解释这种脆弱性。
en_tdlr: Through systematic experiments across multiple datasets, model architectures, and attack methods, this study finds that poor model generalization (large train-test gap) is the strongest indicator of EEG models' vulnerability to membership inference attacks, with longer training and larger models also increasing risk, while no specific characteristics of EEG data consistently explain this vulnerability.
